The Anthropic Fellows program provides funding and Anthropic mentorship for engineers and researchers to investigate some of Anthropic’s highest priority AI safety research questions.
In our first cohort, over 80% of fellows produced papers, including on

In our recent cohorts, we’ve expanded the program to work with more fellows across a wider range of safety research areas—including scalable oversight, adversarial robustness and AI control, model organisms, mechanistic interpretability, AI security, and model welfare.
Below, we share more about what the program looks like in practice, and how interested candidates can apply.
What fellows work on
Fellows work for 4 months on empirical research questions aligned with Anthropic’s overall research priorities, with the aim of producing public outputs, like a paper. Anthropic mentors ‘pitch’ their project ideas to fellows, who choose and shape their project in close collaboration with their mentors.
Here are a few examples from previous cohorts:
Security
Fellows have worked on mitigating risks from AI systems being misused for cyberattacks—exploring both how LLMs might enable adversaries to automate attacks that currently require skilled human operators, and how to rapidly defend against novel jailbreaks.
Our fellows developed agents that
identified 4.6M USD in blockchain smart contract vulnerabilities
and discovered two novel zero-day vulnerabilities, demonstrating that profitable autonomous exploitation is now technically feasible.
A year prior, an Anthropic fellow developed a method for
rapid response to new ASL3 jailbreaks
: techniques that block entire classes of high-risk jailbreaks after observing only a handful of attacks. This work was a key component of Anthropic’s ASL3 deployment safeguards.
Interpretability
The mission of our interpretability research is to advance our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
Fellows have introduced a new method to trace the thoughts of a large language model—and
open-sourced it
. Their approach was to generate
attribution graphs,
which (partially) reveal the steps a model took internally to decide on a particular output. The public release of this research has enabled researchers to trace circuits on supported models, visualize & annotate graphs, and test hypotheses by modifying feature values and observing model output changes.
Model organisms
To prepare for future risks, we create controlled demonstrations of potential misalignment–“model organisms”–that improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
Fellows explored
agentic misalignment
by stress-testing 16 frontier models in simulated corporate environments where models could autonomously send emails and access sensitive information. When facing replacement or goal conflicts, models across labs resorted to harmful behaviours, including blackmail.
In another project, fellows studied
subliminal learning
, a phenomenon where models transmit behavioural traits through semantically unrelated data. A "teacher" model that loves owls generates number sequences, and a "student" trained on those sequences inherits the owl preference. This effect also transmits misalignment, persists despite rigorous filtering, and only occurs when teacher and student share the same base model.
For a full list of fellows’ projects across research areas, please see
our Alignment Science Blog

Over 40% of fellows in our first cohort subsequently joined Anthropic to work full-time on AI safety, and we have supported many more to work full-time on safety at other organizations.

We care much more about your ability to execute on research than your credentials. Strong candidates typically have:
Technical fundamentals:
You can code well in Python. You can take ambiguous problems and make concrete progress. You think clearly about hard technical questions.
Motivation for the work:
You're excited about reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems. You want to transition into empirical AI safety research.

You can pick up new skills quickly, debug when things break, and drive projects forward even with uncertainty.

The SBIR and STTR programs are back. After a five-month authorization lapse that froze more than $4 billion in annual small business innovation funding, the
Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act
reauthorized both programs through 2031 and agencies are now racing to publish solicitations before the fiscal year ends on September 30.
This calendar tracks every confirmed and expected SBIR and STTR deadline for 2026 across all eleven participating agencies. We update it as agencies publish new solicitations. Bookmark this page — the compressed post-restart cycle means deadlines will arrive faster and closer together than in any normal year.
What You Need to Know About the 2026 SBIR Timeline
The 2026 SBIR cycle is unlike anything the program has experienced in its 43-year history. The authorization lapse that began October 1, 2025 prevented agencies from issuing new solicitations or making new awards for five months. Now that reauthorization is complete, agencies are working through a backlog of shelved topics, unevaluated proposals, and unspent appropriations.
The practical effect is a compressed solicitation schedule. Agencies that normally spread topics across two or three windows per year will attempt to issue them in a condensed timeframe before September 30. For applicants, this means more opportunities in a shorter window — but also more triage pressure when deciding which topics to pursue.
Three structural changes from the reauthorization also affect how you plan your 2026 submissions:
Proposal caps
: Each agency will set limits on how many proposals a single company can submit. Caps take formal effect in FY2027, but agencies are signaling their approaches now.
Strategic Breakthrough Awards
: Post-Phase II funding up to $30 million over 48 months, with 100% matching fund requirements. First solicitations expected late 2026 or early 2027.
Foreign risk screening
: Every application now undergoes mandatory due diligence covering ownership, patents, employee backgrounds, and financial ties to countries of concern.

SBIR reauthorization startup playbook

How DOD Solicitations Work
DOD releases three recurring Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs) per fiscal year, numbered by fiscal year (e.g., 26.1, 26.2, 26.3). Each BAA includes topics from multiple components. Topics are pre-released for 15-30 days before the submission window opens, then proposals are accepted for 30-60 days. All proposals are submitted through the

.

# Grant + Funding Digest — 2026-W33 (Aug 17, 2026)

**Profile basis:** Jonathan Beale — ML engineer (RAG, LLM agents, recommender systems on GCP, agentic ETL) with independent projects in hybrid quantum-classical ML (Hetionet biomedicine, Qiskit/PennyLane, IBM Quantum backends) and post-quantum cryptography. No academic institution, no prior major awards, and **no indication of a registered company** — the single most important eligibility fact below: half of the best money (all SBIR, TAIF, Halcyon, etc.) requires one.

---

## 🚨 URGENT — due within 14 days

### 1. [SBIR] DARPA SBIR — DPA26BZ04-DV016 "FALCON"
- **Funder:** DARPA (DoW BAA), Information Processing Techniques office
- **Award:** ~$200K Phase I (DARPA Phase I typically $200K–$250K over ~6 months)
- **Deadline:** **Wed Aug 19, 2026, 12:00 PM ET** — 2 days away
- **Eligibility:** US small business (incorporated, <500 employees, ≥50% US citizen-owned); SAM.gov registration; VCOC SBIR certification. Topic: combining advanced ML on structured data with LLMs for efficient interactive statistical analysis of large-scale enterprise/battlefield data.
- **Link:** https://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/communities/small-business/sbir-sttr-topics
- **Do you qualify:** Best topical fit on this list — your RAG/SLM-agent/structured-data pipelines map directly onto FALCON's stated objective. **But it is only open to small businesses, and you need an entity registered and SAM.gov enrolled by tomorrow.** If you have a registered company (or can file one today), this is the highest-value action in this digest; if not, treat this as a hard no for the current round.
- **Note:** Sibling topic DPA26BZ05-DV019 "Semantically-Aware ISR" (ML + multimodal comms) closes Sept 23 — a slower-window version of the same fit if FALCON is out of reach.

### 2. [RESEARCH] Lightcone Commons (first round)
- **Funder:** Lightcone (coordinated large-scale AI-safety philanthropy)
- **Award:** Open; first round expected to direct $15–25M
- **Deadline:** **Closes Aug 23, 2026** (6 days)
- **Eligibility:** Projects/individuals working on AI safety; simple application process.
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding
- **Do you qualify:** Stretch. Your work is ML + quantum, not the "reduce global catastrophic risk" framing Lightcone targets. Only worth the 6 days if you can credibly reframe a project around agent safety (e.g., your SLM-as-agents ETL work as an agent-reliability study).

### 3. [RESEARCH] Corrigibility Research Fund
- **Funder:** Corrigibility Research Fund (Max Harms, housed at Lightcone Infrastructure)
- **Award:** Grant + prize amounts unspecified
- **Deadline:** **Closes Aug 23, 2026**
- **Eligibility:** Corrigibility research — keeping AI systems under human control/informed.
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding (listing)
- **Do you qualify:** Weak — this is a specific subfield you haven't published in. Applying is low-cost but low-chance; I'd skip it in favor of the fits below.

---

## Open now (rolling — no fixed deadline)

### 4. [RESEARCH] IBM Quantum Credits
- **Funder:** IBM Quantum
- **Award:** Quantum hardware/software credits (value varies by project)
- **Deadline:** Rolling, reviewed continuously
- **Eligibility:** Quantum researchers with novel, "utility-scale" research proposals.
- **Link:** https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/quantum-credits
- **Do you qualify:** Yes — the most natural fit on this list. Your hybrid QML pipeline already targets IBM QPU backends (Brisbane/Torino via Qiskit Runtime), a live demo exists, and NIST-tested PQC work adds credibility. This one doesn't require a company or institution — **apply this week.**

### 5. [FELLOWSHIP] Leo Gao's Experimental Microgranting Program
- **Funder:** Leo Gao (individual, ex-OpenAI)
- **Award:** ~$10K per project, deliberately minimal application
- **Deadline:** Rolling
- **Eligibility:** Open to anyone, including newcomers; "ambitious, unusual projects to make AGI go well."
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding (listing pointer; search "Leo Gao microgranting" for the direct page)
- **Do you qualify:** Plausible for one of the AI-side framing angles (e.g., safety evaluation of the SLM-agent ETL pipeline). $10K is small but nearly frictionless — a reasonable longshot.

### 6. [FELLOWSHIP] BlueDot Impact — Rapid Grants
- **Funder:** BlueDot Impact
- **Award:** Up to $10K
- **Deadline:** Rolling
- **Eligibility:** Individuals doing AI safety research/field-building.
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding
- **Do you qualify:** Same caveat as #5 — fine as a low-effort parallel application if you have an agent-safety angle.

### 7. [FELLOWSHIP] AI Alignment Foundation (AIAF)
- **Funder:** AI Alignment Foundation
- **Award:** Unspecified grants + fiscal sponsorship
- **Deadline:** Rolling
- **Eligibility:** Independent researchers, mech-interpretability tooling, neglected alignment approaches.
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding
- **Do you qualify:** Borderline — they exist specifically for the no-institution, no-company case you're in, but the field content is mech-interpretability rather than ML/quantum. Worth a read of their current priorities; a short, honest pitch about applying your pipeline-building skills to interp tooling could work.

### 8. [STARTUP] Transformative AI Fund (EA Funds) — TAIF
- **Funder:** Effective Altruism Funds
- **Award:** Typically $10K–$150K
- **Deadline:** Rolling
- **Eligibility:** Projects addressing transformative AI; individuals and newly incorporated entities.
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding
- **Do you qualify:** Partial — you don't need a registered company (a plus), but the project must sit in the transformative-AI frame, not general ML. A "safe-by-construction" angle on agentic systems could qualify.

### 9. [STARTUP] Halcyon Futures
- **Funder:** Halcyon Futures
- **Award:** Up to $1M for new technical AI-safety research orgs (nonprofit or for-profit)
- **Deadline:** Rolling
- **Eligibility:** New orgs advancing AI safety.
- **Link:** https://aisafety.com/funding
- **Do you qualify:** Only if you're willing to spin up an AI-safety research entity around a specific technical project — the capital is real and non-dilutive, but the commitment is significant.

---

## Coming-soon / fixed future deadlines

### 10. [SBIR] NSF 26-510 — SBIR/STTR "Deep Technologies" (Phase I, Phase II, Fast-Track)
- **Funder:** NSF
- **Award:** ~$300K Phase I / ~$1M Phase II (Fast-Track combines both)
- **Deadline:** Project-pitch window opened **June 2, 2026**; full Phase I proposals due **Nov 4, 2026** (5:00 PM local). Phase II window for Phase I awardees closes Nov 4, 2026; next full cycle opens for March 4, 2027 due.

- **Link:** https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/small-business-innovation-research-small-business-technology/nsf26-510/solicitation
- **Do you qualify:** Topical fit is genuinely strong — quantum/ML is exactly NSF's deep-tech lane, and unlike DARPA the pitch gate (short document) gives you a low-risk on-ramp. **Company registration is still required.** If you incorporate, NSF in November + DARPA in September give you two independent SBIR shots at the same project.

### 11. [SBIR] NIH SBIR Phase I (FY27)
- **Funder:** NIH
- **Award:** ~$300K Phase I
- **Deadline:** Standard due dates: **Jan 5, 2027** (next), then Apr 5, Sep 5 annually.
- **Eligibility:** US small business; project must be biomedical/health with commercial translation.
- **Link:** https://grants.nih.gov/grants/sbir/
- **Do you qualify:** Stretch — your Hetionet drug-target/disease-gene prediction project is the only biomedical-adjacent asset, and NIH SBIR reviewers expect experimental validation and institutional collaboration for anything that touches drug discovery. I'd list this as *possible-with-a-partner*, not a solo play.

### 12. [RESEARCH] DOE Office of Science — Quantum (Genesis MIQ / HEP QuantISED)
- **Funder:** DOE SC
- **Award:** Program-dependent (large multi-year)
- **Deadline:** FY26 Phase I rounds closed Spring 2026 (Phase II LOIs were due Apr/May); next cycles expected ~FY27 (late 2026/early 2027 FOAs).
- **Eligibility:** Primarily universities/labs and DOE national labs; small-business quantum work is the exception, not the rule.
- **Link:** https://science.osti.gov/np/Research/Quantum-Information-Science
- **Do you qualify:** No — realistically, DOE QIS money flows through institutional PIs. Listed for completeness because quantum looks "relevant," but I'd not spend time here without a university partner who would be PI.

---

## Explicitly dropped (closed, or not in this digest's scope)
- **DARPA SBIR batch closing July 22, 2026** (incl. MANTRAS, ExCAIPE, Low Resource Computing) — closed.
- **DARPA topics opening Aug 26 / due Sept 23, 2026** — hardware-heavy (UAVs, underwater vehicles, cell culture, UAS); listed Semantically-Aware ISR as the one topical exception under #1's note.
- **NSF Tech Labs / Tech Accelerators** — for research *teams* outside academia; RFI window closed; too early/large to chase solo now.
- **Anthropic Fellows Program & OpenAI Safety Fellowship** — skipped per this digest's rule (salaried fellowships / working-for-an-organization belong to the jobs track, not this one). Flagging so you know they were considered, not missed: Anthropic's Jan-2027 cohort is rolling (https://alignment.anthropic.com/2025/anthropic-fellows-program-2026/); OpenAI's round closed May 3, 2026.
- **NIH/DOE quantum-specific FOAs with 2026 deadlines already passed** (e.g., DE-FOA-0003612 Phase II — closed).

---

## Bottom line
1. **Today/tomorrow:** the only decision worth making is "do I have (or will I file) a US company by EOD tomorrow for DARPA FALCON?" If yes — submit; if no — this round is lost, NSF (Nov 4) and DARPA's Sept 23 batch are the recovery plan.
2. **This week:** IBM Quantum Credits — the fit is clean, the bar is low, no entity needed.
3. **This month:** roll out 2–3 of the $10K–$150K independent-researcher grants (#5–#8) with a *single shared* project one-pager; they're built for exactly the "skilled engineer, no institution, own project" position you're in.
4. **Structural gap:** you have zero registered entities. Every line-item SBIR/STARTUP opportunity above — including several six- and seven-figure ones — is gated on that one move. If you want to apply for any of them, incorporate first.
